**Observation Log:**

[TEMPORAL] Session Date: 2023/04/14 (Fri) 22:42  
[FACT] User is inquiring about Capital Gains Tax (CGT) and Business Asset Disposal Relief (BADR).  
[RELATIONSHIP] User has a brother who may also qualify for BADR.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The £1 million lifetime limit for Business Asset Disposal Relief (BADR) applies on an individual basis, not at the company level.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Each individual shareholder who qualifies for the relief has their own separate £1 million allowance.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Both the user and their brother could potentially reduce the rate of Capital Gains Tax (CGT) to 10% on up to £1 million of qualifying gains each.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The £1 million limit is a lifetime limit covering all qualifying disposals made throughout life.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] If previously claimed BADR on other disposals, the user needs to consider any remaining balance in their lifetime limit.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] It is essential to consult with a qualified tax advisor to discuss specific circumstances and determine eligibility for BADR.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] A single shareholder can dispose of their shares and claim BADR even if the business continues to trade.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The relief applies to individual shareholders who meet the qualifying conditions.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] To qualify for BADR, the company must be a trading company or the holding company of a trading group.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The shareholder must hold at least 5% of the ordinary shares and voting rights in the company for at least 24 months before the disposal.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The shareholder must be an officer or employee of the company or a member of its trading group for at least 24 months before the disposal.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] As long as the conditions are met, the individual shareholder may be eligible for BADR on the disposal of their shares.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The position of a company secretary is generally considered sufficient to meet the criterion for being an officer of the company when claiming BADR.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] A company secretary is a recognized officer of a company under UK law and has various legal responsibilities and duties.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] As a company secretary, the user would typically satisfy the third condition for BADR, assuming they meet the other qualifying conditions.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] It is always recommended to consult with a qualified tax advisor to discuss specific circumstances and ensure that all conditions for BADR are met.
